A warm welcome from
Our Headteacher
St Mary Cray Primary Academy is set on the boundary of Orpington and enjoys views out towards Lullingstone. With the look and feel of a village school, we strive to create a calm caring environment for all of our children to learn and thrive.
Our school follows three values of Ambition, Collaboration and Equity and expects the best for our students.
What’s special about St Mary Cray Primary School?​​​​​​​
At St Mary Cray Primary School, we exist to inspire our community, empower children with the agency to succeed and shape aspirational futures.
Village School
We are a one-form entry school on the edge of Orpington, and that 'village school' feel is exactly what we believe makes us special - every child is known and cared for, every face is familiar, and we all grow together.
Outdoor Learning
All children in EYFS and KS1 access our outdoor learning environment once a week. During this time, they are encouraged to build confidence, resilience, and develop hands-on skills alongside their peers.

pageCache.pageTitle: St. Mary Cray Primary Academy - Our Vision
pageCache.text:
Our School
Our Vision
No Barriers to Excellence
Our vision is to develop well-rounded, confident and responsible children who aspire to achieve their full potential. We aim to do this in a welcoming, safe, supportive and inclusive environment where all achievements are celebrated.
Together, we strive to create an educational community of respect and inclusion, empowering all to embrace learning, achieve excellence and transform lives.
Our school ethos is embedded in our vision and values.
Our Values
Our School Values form the priorities that underpin our curriculum design. We believe that by focussing on our school values, our children will be prepared and ready to meet the challenges of the next steps of their education and life so that they can achieve their personal best.
Ambition
At St Mary Cray Primary School, ambition means striving to be the very best we can be in all areas of school life. We encourage every child to set high expectations for themselves, to embrace challenges, and to persevere when things feel difficult. Ambition is not just about achieving excellent academic results, but also about developing creativity, confidence, kindness and resilience. We want our children to dream big, work hard and believe that there are no boundaries to what they can achieve.
Collaboration
At St Mary Cray Primary School, collaboration means working together with respect, kindness and understanding. We believe that learning is most powerful when children support and encourage one another, share ideas and celebrate each other’s successes. Collaboration helps our pupils to develop teamwork, communication and problem-solving skills, preparing them to contribute positively both in school and in the wider community. By working in partnership with families, staff and the trust, we show our children that together we can achieve more.
Equity
At St Mary Cray Primary School, equity means ensuring that every child gets the support, opportunities and challenge they need to succeed. We recognise that each pupil is unique, with different strengths and starting points, and we are committed to removing barriers so that all children can thrive. Equity is about fairness – giving every child what they need, rather than treating everyone the same – so that all pupils can achieve their very best and feel valued within our school community.

pageCache.pageTitle: St. Mary Cray Primary Academy - Welcome from our Headteacher
pageCache.text:
Our School
Welcome from our Headteacher
On behalf of all the staff and pupils here, I am incredibly proud to welcome you to St Mary Cray Primary Academy.
St Mary Cray Primary Academy is a vibrant community school where every child is known, valued, and encouraged to flourish. Nestled on the edge of Orpington, the school offers a warm 'village' feel where every face is familiar, and everyone grows together.
The bedrock of the school is built on three core principles: Respect, Resilience, and Responsibility. High standards and traditional values are at the heart of daily life, instilling a sense of pride, integrity, and self-management that serves children well as they mature into independent, confident young people with the agency to succeed. The shared ambition across the school community is simple yet powerful: to leave the badge and the local community in a better place.
A holistic approach ensures that while academic achievement is a central focus, children truly thrive because they feel safe, happy, and included. Safeguarding and inclusion are at the heart of everything we do, sitting alongside a dynamic curriculum designed to spark curiosity – whether in the classroom, through outdoor learning, across extracurricular clubs, or during educational visits.
As a proud member of The Spring Partnership Trust, St Mary Cray works closely with neighbouring schools, living out the shared values of Ambition, Collaboration, and Equity to ensure there are no barriers to excellence for any child.
Having served as the heart of this community for over a century, the school deeply values its partnership with families. The ultimate goal is to nurture kind, well-rounded individuals who are ready to make a positive impact on the world around them.
Visitors are always warmly welcomed to experience St Mary Cray Primary in action and see firsthand what makes it such a special place to learn and grow.
Mrs Tanya Artmann - Acting Headteacher

pageCache.text:
Clubs
External & Staff-Run Clubs
In order to provide a variety of after school activities, we have sought out the expertise of external companies. Each club is bookable directly via the company; please see the clubs timetable below or contact the school office for more information as these providers and clubs may also change on a termly basis.
To book your child onto a club you simply need to contact the company directly; further details are shown below. Clubs spaces are limited and offered on a first-come -first-served basis, so we urge you to respond quickly.
Extracurricular clubs are a third party provider to the school that are charged a letting fee for the rental of school premises on a commercial basis. Enrolment to an external club is voluntary and the contract is between the parent and the provider. All lettings are subject to relevant due diligence including safeguarding and risk assessment policies.
As extracurricular clubs (before school, lunchtimes and after school) are external, please note that information held by the school such as medical information, allergies and any pertinent information with regards to collections is not passed to the clubs from the school due to GDPR. It is therefore the parents responsibility to ensure that the third party provider has all the information they need to ensure the safety of your child whilst in their care.

pageCache.pageTitle: St. Mary Cray Primary Academy - PE and Sports Premium
pageCache.text:
Our School
PE and Sports Premium
St Mary Cray Primary Academy PE and Sports Premium Grant Information
What is PE and Sport Premium?
The Primary PE and Sport Premium was introduced in March 2013 to improve the provision of physical education and school sport in primary schools across England. The £150 million per year funding is provided jointly by the Departments for Education, Health, and Culture, Media and Sport (DfE, DH, DCMS). The funding is allocated directly to primary schools and is ring-fenced. This means it may only be spent on improving the provision of PE and sport in schools. In February 2014 the government committed to continue the funding until 2020.
How much funding does St Mary Cray Primary School receive?
Annually, we receive £16,000 plus £10 per pupil on roll and have done since 2017/2018; before this we were entitled to £8000 plus £5 per pupil. This funding is ring-fenced to ensure that in impacts directly on the development of subject knowledge, skill acquisition, agility, balance, co-ordination and physical fitness of the pupils here. We aim to use the funding, in it`s entirety, to raise the profile of PE and Sport throughout the school and produce a sustainable legacy that will benefit the pupils of this school for many years to come.
Please refer to https://www.gov.uk/guidance/pe-and-sport-premium-for-primary-schools for payment dates.

pageCache.pageTitle: St. Mary Cray Primary Academy - Forest School
pageCache.text:
Learning Excellence
Forest School
Outdoor learning is very important to us at St Mary Cray Primary School. We have two fantastic Forest Schools. One on our own site, and the other at another Trust school which we get to visit regularly. At our on-site Forest School, we offer cross-curricular learning to children across the year groups from Reception upwards, including working with tools, having fires and creating art. Learning to work together, helping and supporting each other, problem-solving and taking (supervised and calculated) risks are vital parts of children's learning.
Children in Reception are provided with waterproof trousers and jackets, as well as Wellington boots. Older year groups should provide their own wet/cold weather clothes as we go out in all weathers.

pageCache.pageTitle: St. Mary Cray Primary Academy - Pupil Leadership
pageCache.text:
Learning Excellence
Pupil Leadership
Pupil Voice
The children in our school are the most important people.
As such, they have lots of opportunities to share their thoughts on school issues – both formally and informally. Mr Frost's door is always open for both children and adults.
Opportunities for Pupil Leadership
There are so many opportunities for Pupil Leadership at St Mary Cray Primary. We have a fantastic Head Boy and Head Girl who support the running of the school, including taking our parent tours on Open Days, presenting awards in assembly and representing the school community at events.
We also have children supporting in the following roles:
Oracy champions
Sustainability champions
Lunchtime hall helpers
Litter pickers
Library helpers
School Council
The main aim of the School Council is to help to make our school a better place for the children and to give us an opportunity to have their opinions and ideas heard. Each class from Year Two upwards has two representatives who are elected every year.
Our Council meet to discuss what their class' opinions are and to suggest ways that the school can improve how we work and what is offer to children.
The class representatives tell the children in their classes what has been discussed at each meeting and the children can ask the representatives to take forward their ideas to the next meeting.
Anti-Bullying Ambassadors
The anti-bullying ambassador team has the aim of ensuring that all children feel safe and happy in school. This includes inside the school building and while on the playground. They are play leaders and friendship ambassadors.
Junior Cray Forum
This is a group of 4 children from year 5 who work alongside Midfield Primary School, Leesons Primary School and Poverest Primary School to engage in local community projects to protect the future of the area.
TfL Explorers Ambassadors (TEAs)
Children in year 4 and 5 are chosen to be ambassadors for the school to support children travelling safely to and from school, and support with how we travel when outside of school. Projects and competitions are coordinated across the borough.
Cookie Policy

pageCache.pageTitle: St. Mary Cray Primary Academy - What to do if you are worried about a child
pageCache.text:
Safeguarding
What to do if you are worried about a child
St Mary Cray Primary Academy is committed to safeguarding and promoting the wellbeing of all children and we expect all staff, volunteers and visitors to share this commitment.
We are aware that child abuse can happen to all children regardless of gender, culture, religion, social background or disability.
If you become concerned about:
Please inform the Designated Safeguarding Lead or one of the members of the Safeguarding team (see here).
If you feel a child may be at risk of harm but you are not sure then inform the DSL who will provide advice and take appropriate action.
Concerns can also be reported by emailing safeguarding@st-marycray.bromley.sch.uk. Concerns can also be reported in school, please ask a member of staff for a reporting form and hand it to the DSL; you should ideally have a verbal conversation in the first instance. All concerns are retained in order (known as a chronology of events) to determine patterns and provide detailed information as well as evidence of action taken.
Members of staff can report concerns directly to the safeguarding team via SafeGuard.
something a child says
marks, bruises, cuts or other physical injuries
What do I do if a child discloses they are being harmed?
The NSPCC offer great advice and a video on how to respond to disclosures of abuse here.
Types of Harm
Everybody has a responsibility to keep all children under 18 safe. Harm can be identified in the following ways:
Physical
When a child is deliberately hurt or injured. This includes female genital mutilation. Any person who expects that a child has been subjected to FGM has a legal responsibility to report this to the Police and must also inform the DSL immediately.
Sexual
This is when a child is influenced or forced to take part in a sexual activity. This could be a physical activity or non physical e.g. being influenced, exposed to or made to look at an inappropriate image. This includes child sexual exploitation.
Emotional
This is when a child is made to feel frightened, worthless or unloved. It can occur through intimidation (e.g. shouting at), using threats or making fun of someone. It might also occur when children see their parents, families or visitors to the home, fighting, arguing or using other forms of violence.
Neglect
This is when a child is not being taken care of by their parents/carers. It can relate to poor hygiene, poor diet, not keeping appointments for health or additional needs, not coming to school or being left without supervision by a suitable adult.
Extremism and Radicalisation
The holding of extreme views which do not reflect British Values:
democracy
the rule of law
individual liberty
Cyber
Where the Internet is used to coerce, bully or exploit a child. Where children are allowed access to unsuitable images, references or articles.
